filterQueryInput.description: A cmdk-powered structured query input that maps free text and field:value tokens to portable filter clauses.
filterQueryInput.suggestionBehaviorBody: Filters lists unused fields. Values lists candidates for the field at the caret and preserves earlier multi-select values. Recent searches contains only successfully committed queries, is filtered by the current draft, and remains separate from facet values or server requests.
filterQueryInput.reuseBody: Replace fields and queryFields to change the business vocabulary, aliases, ordering, and suggested filters without forking the UI. The query string remains a projection of the controlled filter clauses.
filterQueryInput.codecBody: Replace codec when another product needs a different text grammar. Use freeText to map unqualified words to one application field while keeping structured tokens available.
filterQueryInput.headlessBody: Use the headless hook when the host product needs its own input, listbox, or positioning layer. Parsing, clause reconciliation, history, and commit behavior remain shared.
filterQueryInput.headlessPreview: The headless core can drive any input and suggestion surface.
filterQueryInput.p0: Business filter model. It is shared with FilterBuilder and contains no table dependency.
filterQueryInput.p1: Controls query keys, aliases, display order, and whether a field appears in suggestions.
filterQueryInput.p2: Controlled committed clauses. Draft text is kept separate until a valid commit.
filterQueryInput.p3: Receives committed clauses and the reason, represented clause IDs, and preserved unsupported clauses.
filterQueryInput.p4: Optional parser and serializer replacement for a different query grammar.
filterQueryInput.p5: Maps bare text tokens to one field; set false to require structured tokens only.
filterQueryInput.p6: Controls when a valid draft updates committed clauses.
filterQueryInput.p7: Preserves clauses the current codec cannot serialize by default.
filterQueryInput.p9: Set false to disable the default Meta+K / Control+K opener, or provide accepted shortcut labels.
filterQueryInput.p10: Async, application-owned suggestions such as saved searches or AI assistance; they can replace the current token or filters.
filterQueryInput.p11: Replace local visuals without changing parsing or keyboard behavior. Use the headless hook for a different DOM structure.
filterQueryInput.p12: Allow several field conditions in one submitted query. Set false to allow only one condition.
filterQueryInput.asyncHistoryBody: A field may load server-filtered values and counts through loadSuggestions. History remains opt-in: use the SSR-safe hook and spread its controlled props into the component.
filterQueryInput.asyncHistoryPreview: The example shows the two opt-in extension points; no browser storage is touched unless the history hook is used.
filterQueryInput.manualInputHint: Click the search field, type one or more conditions separated by spaces, then press Enter:
